newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: REINZ attacks RBNZ for interventionist approach.
newsitem.headline: REINZ attacks RBNZ for interventionist approach.

text.p: The Real Estate Institute of New Zealand on Friday attacked the Reserve Bank of New Zealand for its interventionist approach to managing monetary policy.

"The Reserve Bank is taking a highly interventionist approach by saying they don't want banks lowering their rates in May only to have to put them back up again in June," said REINZ President Colin Brown.
"We believe the market should be allowed to find its own level," he said.
"We accept that the governor of the Reserve Bank must apply his monetary policy as he sees fit, but on a quarterly basis, not weekly or daily," he said.
Brown said the RBNZ should not hinder growing competition between banks and emerging non-bank mortgage lenders.

"We believe recent mortgage interest rate falls are a response to increased competition between bank and non-bank lenders and that therefore it is unfortunate for the Reserve Bank to be intervening in that process."
Brown said banks had been sitting on big margins for too long at the expense of homeowners.
"Now non-bank lenders are getting involved in the mortgage market, margins are coming back as lending becomes more competitive.
"But the Reserve Bank is effectively intervening in an important aspect of market competition. So whose side is the Reserve Bank on?" Brown said.
RBNZ governor Don Brash issued a statement on Wednesday rejecting criticism the bank was flip-flopping over monetary policy.
"Our view of desired conditions has not changed since December," he said.
